items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra for ChatGPT Work, Codex, and API
facts: GPT-6.1 Terra is a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing.
Its standard API prices are 50% lower than those of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol.
Starting today, GPT-6.1 Terra is available to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Developers can also access it through the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-terra.
Standard API pricing is $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens, and $5 per million output tokens.

At medium reasoning effort on Agents’ Last Exam, GPT-6.1 Terra scores 15 percentage points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra at about one-third the cost. It even performs on par with GPT-6 Astra at only one-tenth its price per token.
At maximum reasoning effort on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT‑6.1 Terra solves 50.3% of tasks, more than double GPT‑5.6 Terra’s published score of 21.5%.

items.title: Cursor announces Agent SDK for defining agents as code
facts: The Agent SDK is now available.
Define agents as code, with prompts in Markdown and tools in TypeScript.
Deploy them on our hosted infrastructure, or run them on your own.
Built-in evals let you measure every change and make your agents better over time.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.311 adds self-hosted runner idle options and other fixes
facts: Added --hold-idle-file and --max-hold-min to self-hosted-runner, to keep an idle session while your host reports processes it left running
Added a tip for the Explanatory output style, shown when you ask Claude for explanations
[VSCode] Added syntax coloring to code blocks in Claude’s replies, in light, dark and high contrast dark themes

Changed ultrathink in the interactive terminal to run its turn at xhigh effort on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 through Anthropic’s API; typed while Claude is working, it raises the rest of that turn
Fixed standard-context sessions stopping with “Usage credits required for 1M context” when a request ran over 200K tokens; Claude Code now compacts the conversation and continues
